2270	// gcSeries removes the provided series from the head index and updates head metrics,
2271	// postings, tombstones and WAL expiries accordingly. shouldEvict is the per-series predicate
2272	// applied after the safety check for series that received fresh samples since the caller
2273	// collected the ref list.
2274	//
2275	// The returned references are the series that got deleted.
2276	func (h *Head) gcSeries(seriesRefs []storage.SeriesRef, maxt int64, shouldEvict func(*memSeries) bool) map[storage.SeriesRef]struct{} {
2277		// Drop old chunks and remember series IDs and hashes if they can be
2278		// deleted entirely.
2279		deleted, affected, chunksRemoved, staleSeriesDeleted := h.series.gcSeries(seriesRefs, maxt, shouldEvict)
2280		seriesRemoved := len(deleted)
2281	
2282		h.metrics.seriesRemoved.Add(float64(seriesRemoved))
2283		h.metrics.chunksRemoved.Add(float64(chunksRemoved))
2284		h.metrics.chunks.Sub(float64(chunksRemoved))
2285		h.numSeries.Sub(uint64(seriesRemoved))
2286		h.numStaleSeries.Sub(uint64(staleSeriesDeleted))
2287	
2288		// Remove deleted series IDs from the postings lists.
2289		h.postings.Delete(deleted, affected)
2290	
2291		// Remove tombstones referring to the deleted series.
2292		h.tombstones.DeleteTombstones(deleted)
2293	
2294		if h.wal != nil {
2295			h.walExpiriesMtx.Lock()
2296			// Keep series records until we're past timestamp maxt
2297			// because the WAL will still have samples records with
2298			// this ref ID. If we didn't keep these series records then
2299			// on start up when we replay the WAL, or any other code
2300			// that reads the WAL, wouldn't be able to use those
2301			// samples since we would have no labels for that ref ID.
2302			for ref := range deleted {
2303				h.walExpiries[chunks.HeadSeriesRef(ref)] = maxt
2304			}
2305			h.walExpiriesMtx.Unlock()
2306		}
2307	
2308		return deleted
2309	}

2311	// deleteSeriesByID deletes the series with the given reference.
2312	// Only used for WAL replay.
2313	func (h *Head) deleteSeriesByID(refs []chunks.HeadSeriesRef) {
2314		var (
2315			deleted            = map[storage.SeriesRef]struct{}{}
2316			affected           = map[labels.Label]struct{}{}
2317			staleSeriesDeleted = 0
2318			chunksRemoved      = 0
2319		)
2320	
2321		for _, ref := range refs {
2322			// Delete the reference from the series map.
2323			// Copying getByID here to avoid locking and unlocking twice.
2324			stripe := h.series.refStripe(ref)
2325			h.series.locks[stripe].Lock()
2326			series := h.series.series[stripe][ref]
2327			if series == nil {
2328				h.series.locks[stripe].Unlock()
2329				continue
2330			}
2331			delete(h.series.series[stripe], series.ref)
2332			h.series.locks[stripe].Unlock()
2333	
2334			// Delete the reference from the hash.
2335			hash := series.lset.Hash()
2336			hashStripe := int(hash) & (h.series.size - 1)
2337			h.series.locks[hashStripe].Lock()
2338			h.series.hashes[hashStripe].del(hash, series.ref)
2339			h.series.locks[hashStripe].Unlock()
2340	
2341			if value.IsStaleNaN(series.lastValue) ||
2342				(series.lastHistogramValue != nil && value.IsStaleNaN(series.lastHistogramValue.Sum)) ||
2343				(series.lastFloatHistogramValue != nil && value.IsStaleNaN(series.lastFloatHistogramValue.Sum)) {
2344				staleSeriesDeleted++
2345			}
2346	
2347			chunksRemoved += len(series.mmappedChunks)
2348			if series.headChunks != nil {
2349				chunksRemoved += series.headChunks.len()
2350			}
2351			if series.headChunkCount.Load() >= 2 {
2352				h.series.decMmapReady(series.ref)
2353			}
2354			// Clear to prevent a double-subtraction from the chunksRemoved gauge if
2355			// resetSeriesWithMMappedChunks is queued on the same WAL-replay processor
2356			// after this deletion (it would otherwise subtract len(mmappedChunks) again).
2357			series.mmappedChunks = nil
2358	
2359			deleted[storage.SeriesRef(series.ref)] = struct{}{}
2360			series.lset.Range(func(l labels.Label) { affected[l] = struct{}{} })
2361		}
2362	
2363		h.metrics.seriesRemoved.Add(float64(len(deleted)))
2364		h.metrics.chunksRemoved.Add(float64(chunksRemoved))
2365		h.metrics.chunks.Sub(float64(chunksRemoved))
2366		h.numSeries.Sub(uint64(len(deleted)))
2367		h.numStaleSeries.Sub(uint64(staleSeriesDeleted))
2368	
2369		// Remove deleted series IDs from the postings lists.
2370		h.postings.Delete(deleted, affected)
2371	
2372		// Remove tombstones referring to the deleted series.
2373		h.tombstones.DeleteTombstones(deleted)
2374	}

2376	// gcSeries walks all series and removes those whose ref is in seriesRefs, whose maxTime is
2377	// <= maxt, and for which shouldEvict returns true. Returns the set of deleted refs, the set
2378	// of label-name/value pairs whose postings are affected, the count of removed chunks, and
2379	// the number of deleted series that carried a stale-NaN last value.
2380	func (s *stripeSeries) gcSeries(seriesRefs []storage.SeriesRef, maxt int64, shouldEvict func(*memSeries) bool) (_ map[storage.SeriesRef]struct{}, _ map[labels.Label]struct{}, _, _ int) {
2381		var (
2382			deleted            = map[storage.SeriesRef]struct{}{}
2383			affected           = map[labels.Label]struct{}{}
2384			rmChunks           = 0
2385			staleSeriesDeleted = 0
2386		)
2387	
2388		refsSet := map[storage.SeriesRef]struct{}{}
2389		for _, ref := range seriesRefs {
2390			refsSet[ref] = struct{}{}
2391		}
2392	
2393		check := func(hashShard int, hash uint64, series *memSeries, deletedForCallback map[chunks.HeadSeriesRef]labels.Labels) {
2394			if _, exists := refsSet[storage.SeriesRef(series.ref)]; !exists {
2395				// This series was not provided by the caller. Skip it.
2396				return
2397			}
2398	
2399			series.Lock()
2400			defer series.Unlock()
2401	
2402			if series.maxTime() > maxt {
2403				return
2404			}
2405	
2406			if !shouldEvict(series) {
2407				return
2408			}
2409	
2410			if series.headChunks != nil {
2411				rmChunks += series.headChunks.len()
2412			}
2413			rmChunks += len(series.mmappedChunks)
2414	
2415			// The series is gone entirely. We need to keep the series lock
2416			// and make sure we have acquired the stripe locks for hash and ID of the
2417			// series alike.
2418			// If we don't hold them all, there's a very small chance that a series receives
2419			// samples again while we are half-way into deleting it.
2420			stripe := s.refStripe(series.ref)
2421			if series.headChunkCount.Load() >= 2 {
2422				s.decMmapReady(series.ref)
2423			}
2424			if hashShard != stripe {
2425				s.locks[stripe].Lock()
2426				defer s.locks[stripe].Unlock()
2427			}
2428	
2429			deleted[storage.SeriesRef(series.ref)] = struct{}{}
2430			if isStaleSeries(series) {
2431				staleSeriesDeleted++
2432			}
2433			series.lset.Range(func(l labels.Label) { affected[l] = struct{}{} })
2434			s.hashes[hashShard].del(hash, series.ref)
2435			delete(s.series[stripe], series.ref)
2436			deletedForCallback[series.ref] = series.lset // OK to access lset; series is locked at the top of this function.
2437		}
2438	
2439		s.iterForDeletion(check)
2440	
2441		return deleted, affected, rmChunks, staleSeriesDeleted
2442	}
2443

units.summary: New test. It evicts a series with CompactSelectedSeries, forces WAL checkpoints with truncateWAL(150), and checks that the evicted series's record is still in the checkpoint because its walExpiry (head maxt 200) has not passed.
units.headline: New test: evicted selected series record stays in WAL checkpoint
units.reason: New test only; it adds coverage and cannot change production behavior.

units.summary: gcStaleSeries is renamed to gcSeries and now takes a shouldEvict predicate. numStaleSeries is now decremented by the number of deleted series that were actually stale, not by every deleted series. On the stale path the result is the same, since every evicted series is stale there. On the selected-series path this stops the stale gauge from being under-counted.
units.headline: Head GC takes eviction predicate; stale counter counts only stale deletions
units.reason: Changes eviction logic and the head's stale-series accounting, which is now shared by two compaction paths.
focus: numStaleSeries is decremented only for series where isStaleSeries is true at eviction time
walExpiries[ref]=maxt is still set for every deleted series on both the stale and the selected path

units.summary: The hardcoded stale-NaN check is replaced by a caller-supplied shouldEvict predicate, which runs under the series lock after the maxTime<=maxt check. The function also returns how many deleted series were stale. The stale path keeps its old semantics because truncateStaleSeries passes isStaleSeries in its predicate.
units.headline: Stripe GC uses pluggable eviction predicate, reports stale deletions
units.reason: Core eviction logic is now generalized, so non-stale series can be removed from the head under locks.
focus: shouldEvict runs with series.Lock held, which hasAppendIDAbove requires
the stale path's predicate still includes isStaleSeries, so CompactStaleHead behaves as before
